guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization code flow for acting on behalf of the current user, with a confidential client, redirect URI and Client ID/secret. The api_v3 scope is the standard API and is the default if no scope is checked. The work package collection endpoint is documented with offset and pageSize pagination. Reading titles depends on the connected person's existing View work packages permission. Customer instance admins must register the OAuth application on each instance, which is a first-test prerequisite. Setup and execution remain untested.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Authorization code flow obtains a user-bound bearer token
findings.detail: The authorization endpoint accepts response_type=code with client_id, redirect_uri and scope, then the token endpoint exchanges the code for a bearer access token and refresh token. Client credentials is a separate flow and is not used for acting as the connected person.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects their own instance and the app acts as the connected person.

findings.title: api_v3 scope for the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope. If no scope is checked when the OAuth application is created, api_v3 is assumed. The scope is broad for the API, and the boundary is what the connected person can see in OpenProject, not a read-only restriction.

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for a user-bound bearer token

steps.title: Read first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: Send a GET with the bearer token to the work package collection with offset=1, pageSize=25 and filters set to an empty JSON array, URL-encoded as %5B%5D, so the default filter is not applied. Expected result is a HAL collection with _embedded.elements, each element having a subject, plus total, count, offset and pageSize. Record total and count for the paging loop. Boundary check: send only this GET; do not call POST, PATCH or DELETE, and confirm the outgoing request log contains no write methods.
steps.doneWhen: The response is 200 with _embedded.elements, each element has a subject, and total, count and pageSize are recorded from the response.

offset The page number that is requested from paginated collection Integer when offset based available
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: bearer token from the authorization code exchange; placeholder only
offset=1: first page number
pageSize=25: page size reused for every page
filters=[]: empty JSON array URL-encoded as %5B%5D to disable the default filter

steps.title: Page through remaining accessible work package titles by offset
steps.detail: Using the same bearer token, pageSize and filters=[] as the first request, repeat the GET with offset increased by one page number each time (2, 3, and so on). Collect subject from each page's _embedded.elements. Stop only when the collected subject count equals total from the first response. An empty page is not a stopping rule. Boundary check: send only GET requests and confirm the outgoing request log contains no POST, PATCH or DELETE calls.
steps.doneWhen: Every offset page from 1 through the page that completes the collection has been requested with filters=[], and the number of collected subjects equals total.
